about: Tessaway Freight's definition registry, added in Part 4. Tessaway Freight is a fictional company and every owner is a fictional role there, not a real person. Each definition keeps the stable id it has in data/DEFINITIONS.md; the version goes up when its meaning changes, and every version stays in its history. 'serves' lists what the context contract hands out under each definition: ontology terms (lookup_definition, resolve_entity), metrics (compute_metric) and rules (check_rule). Every term, metric and rule the contract can serve belongs to exactly one definition (tests/test_registry.py). Written on 2026-10-13, before any Part 4 agent ran.

owners.VP Operations: Runs dispatch, carrier relations and the delivery floor. Decides what counts as a load, a delivery and an on-time delivery, because the customer contracts it signs are measured on them.
owners.Controller: Runs billing, carrier pay and the books. Decides when a load can be billed and what counts as revenue, margin and the reporting currency.
owners.VP Account Management: Runs the account managers. Decides who the customer is when sites, parents and paying offices differ.
owners.Director of Customer Experience: Runs the customer portal. Decides what the portal shows customers, including its own on-time flag.

history.change: First version: a load is one shipment counted once; re-tenders, test and voided rows are not loads; booked on the first tender.
First version: delivered is status DLVD on the final row, dated by arrival at the last stop on the local clock.
First version: billable only with a signed proof of delivery on file; test loads are never billed.

First version: on time at or before the end of the appointment window, local clock; a late load with a shipper-caused delay is left out, neither on time nor late. Names the operations meaning and the portal meaning as not official.
First version: the portal's flag compares delivery date with the requested date; right only for what customers see in the portal.
First version: a customer is a parent account; sites roll up to it; a bill-to party is not the customer.
First version: invoice totals less credit memos plus customer cancel fees, in US dollars, by document date.

Part 7: invoices and credit memos belong to the period the load was delivered (final stop, local clock), not the invoice or credit date; canceled-load fees keep the fee date; amounts and currency unchanged.
